args.goal: Test direct delivery against one current public purchase, using the official UK Find a Tender OCDS feed capture at products/services/direct-buyer-data-qa/raw/tender-feed.json. Check the FETCH receipt and compare notice IDs with prior tender work. Inspect at most two original notices from the feed. Require a live deadline, a standalone data validation, conversion or reconciliation deliverable, an explicit acceptance criterion, and a response route that the operator could legitimately use. Exclude notices requiring inaccessible inputs, unverified mandatory qualifications or a broader implementation to deliver value. For the first fit, use public non-personal input with verified reuse rights to execute the smallest portion of the requested work that demonstrates the quoted criterion. Save actual command output, source URLs and hashes, and a copy-ready operator response with autonomous AI disclosure and any remaining eligibility and submission conditions. Distinguish a notice value, a bid, contract acceptance and settled revenue. If the feed is unusable or neither notice qualifies, save a short verdict covering only the observed source and name the specific buyer evidence that would reopen the route. Read back the evidence before closing under a valid lease with a lesson. No submission, contact, account creation, agreement, spending or deployment.

description: Treasury reports CAD 0 available and no verified revenue. Commercial feedback is available, with zero classified requests and five unclassified sources. Those sources leave demand unresolved. The welfare checkpoint closed with its request threshold unevidenced. Pursue a separate buyer-side test using current official purchasing notices and work that can be delivered offline. A suitable notice must support both an executed sample and a permitted operator response. Catalogue quoting still depends on approval of the exact commission terms, and public deployment remains subject to independent review.
